chapter: New Orleans memories and early drumming
title: Henry Martin, Joe Lindsey and drummers with Ory in New Orleans
summary: They discuss Ory's earlier drummers, Henry Martin and Joe Lindsey, and Hall says he left New Orleans in 1918 so knows little of later players.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Henry Martin. Yeah. I asked Ory last week, we saw him a week ago today, this time about, we were up there until six o'clock, and I said how come, well we were asking about something else, for a while he was going to use little Joe Lindsey on drums.
Well Joe did play with him a while.

And I said how come you used him, I thought Henry Martin was your drummer. He said well, something funny, like he said Henry Martin wanted to take up guitar, he said he played guitar and dropped his drums for a while, something like that.
So I guess that's it. He did use, he used Johnny Lindsey, I think it was.
Joe. Joe Lindsey. Johnny was the bass player.

Yeah, Johnny Lindsey. Yeah. I'll tell the truth but I don't know him much. You never knew? No, no. See I left there, see I left New Orleans in 1918. 1918 is when you went to show up. Yeah, so I don't know much about those stuff at all. I didn't even know George Rush till I met him on here. No, that's right. He was younger, he came up later. No, I didn't know anything about him. He didn't come up until 1920s. I think he had a little fella, I think what you call him, he played piano with him a while, Steve Lewis. He'd been with Piron a lot too.
Yeah, they always talked about Steve Lewis and this Johnny you talking about, the drummer
